game.title: TWO EYES
game.tagline: A daylight study in colour perception
learn.title: Colour is a relationship.
learn.lede: A hue never stands alone. Light, material and the colours around it all shape what you see.
learn.lightCopy: Screens combine red, green and blue light. When all three meet at full intensity, they create white light.
learn.pigmentCopy: Paint absorbs some wavelengths and reflects others. Mixing pigments changes the light that reaches your eye.
learn.valueCopy: Tint adds white, shade adds black and tone softens a hue with grey. Brightness can carry meaning when hue cannot.
colour.kicker: DESIGN FOR MORE THAN ONE VIEW
colour.title: Never let colour do all the talking.
colour.lede: Deuteranopia changes how some reds and greens are perceived. A thoughtful design keeps its meaning visible in every view.
colour.ruleTitle: A colour is never the only clue.
colour.ruleCopy: Pair hue with a shape, a pattern, a label or a clear brightness difference. The information stays legible even when two colours appear alike.
home.copy: Step into a sunlit architectural studio. Join two brothers, Jack and John, as they explore four interactive colour-theory installations and unlock the studio vault.
home.cardCopy: Jack sees the studio in standard trichromatic colour vision. John's view uses an illustrative deuteranopia simulation; shapes, patterns, labels and value contrast remain critical clues.
preview.title: Move through the studio.
preview.copy: W A S D to walk, the mouse to look around, Shift to move faster and E to examine. Press Tab to switch the same studio between Jack's standard colour view and John's illustrative deuteranopia simulation. It is an approximation; colour-vision experiences vary. H shows or hides this guide; Escape pauses.
